title: Minimum days to make M bouquets
pattern: BS on answer with a greedy feasibility check
problemStatement: Given bloom days, make m bouquets of k adjacent flowers each. Find the minimum day, or -1.
intuition: Waiting longer never hurts, so feasibility is monotone in the day. The check is a single sweep counting runs of already-bloomed adjacent flowers.

approaches.title: Optimal: binary search over days
approaches.idea: Feasibility: count complete groups of k consecutive bloomed flowers.
approaches.dryRun:
bloom=[1,10,3,10,2] m=3 k=1 range [1,10]
day=5: bloomed at 1,3,2 -> 3 bouquets, feasible, hi=5
day=3: bloomed 1,3,2 -> 3 feasible, hi=3
day=2: bloomed 1,2 -> 2 < 3, lo=3 -> 3
approaches.whyWorks: Greedily closing a group as soon as k adjacent flowers bloom is optimal for maximising group count.

edgeCases: All flowers bloom on the same day
commonMistakes: Overflow of m*k in fixed-width languages
Counting non-adjacent flowers as a group
Not resetting the run counter on an unbloomed flower
patternRecognition: BS on answer where the check is itself a greedy scan
followUps: What if flowers need not be adjacent?
Maximise bouquets by a fixed day
interviewInsight: The impossible case (m*k > n) is an easy point that many candidates forget.
